subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve distinct ACP child-session parallelism while investigating ACPX/Claude launch readiness, or intentionally serialize/gate rapid distinct ACP spawns?
rationale: Current tests and docs preserve distinct-session parallelism, but the reported failure may only be recoverable through a launch-readiness fix or a product-level concurrency tradeoff after live proof.

options.title: Prove and preserve parallelism
options.body: Run a live two-spawn ACPX/Claude smoke and fix only the confirmed launch-readiness or OpenClaw dispatch boundary while keeping distinct sessions parallel by default.

options.title: Add a deliberate gate
options.body: Choose an explicit per-backend or per-agent ACP spawn serialization policy if maintainers decide reliability is more important than distinct-session parallelism for this path.

options.title: Wait for fresher repro
options.body: Keep the issue in needs-info until a current reporter or maintainer can provide logs proving the failure still occurs on latest release or main.

recommendation.title: Prove and preserve parallelism
recommendation.body: Run a live two-spawn ACPX/Claude smoke and fix only the confirmed launch-readiness or OpenClaw dispatch boundary while keeping distinct sessions parallel by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The ACP spawn/control-plane behavior appears to date to the ACP thread-bound agents work, making this the best available product-boundary owner from history.
